newsitem.title: FRANCE: French first round vote message to Chirac-Seguin.
newsitem.headline: French first round vote message to Chirac-Seguin.

text.p: French National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin said French voters were still awaiting an answer from President Jacques Chirac to the economic problems he set out to solve in 1995.

Seguin, tipped as a possible prime minister if the centre-right wins the second round of a parliamentary election on Sunday, said a combined left lead in the first round of voting was "a message addressed to the president".

French people had great hopes in 1995, the year of the presidential election, that the political establishment would provide an answer to their economic problems which offered a "third way" combining liberalism with the needs of society.
"We have not yet had this answer," he said in an interview with weekly L'Express to be published on Wednesday.
"The policies undertaken since 1995 by Jacques Chirac must be continued in the direction he indicated in the presidential campaign," Seguin said.
Chirac, who has been criticised by opponents for abandoning campaign pledges to make fighting unemployment a priority, was due to address the nation at 1800 GMT on Tuesday.
